thread:
sophia: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on canary this morning. Triton kernel chooser is repeatedly falling back to CUDA/CUTLASS for short-seq (<32) requests on KV-hot routes. p95 latency up ~45ms. Probe/telemetry attached.
perf-bot: alert: routing-fallback-rate spike detected (service=inference, env=canary) :warning:
raj: Can you paste the profiler traces? curious if it's a kernel mismatch or batching smearing.
sophia: quick trace below. this is a hot request pattern (prefix cache hits).
```
PROFILE: model=gpt-7b
seq=16 batch=4 kv_cache=hot
route: triton -> probe -> fallback (cuda_cutlass)
infer_time: triton=120ms, fallback=165ms
kernel: triton-attn v2 vs cutlass-sm75
note: fallback triggers after probe sample shows lower throughput
```
anya: interesting — are we seeing more fallbacks when kv-cache is warm? that could bias probe samples since cached requests are cheaper in triton path.
kevin: my hunch: hysteresis window and probe sampling weight are too aggressive on short sequences. small seqs have low amortized kernel startup cost so cutlass can look better for a handful of samples.
kevin: suggest tweaking config:
```
{"probe_samples": 100, "probe_window_ms": 120000, "hysteresis_ms": 50, "min_seq_for_cutlass": 32}
```
bri: FYI, the new autotune rollout from last week lowered probe_samples to 20 to speed decisions. rollover helped for long-seq workloads but may be causing oscillation on short-seq KV-hot traffic.
sophia: also seeing divergence between H100 and A10 nodes — H100 shows higher fallback rate on the same traffic. likely kernel selection cost model needs arch-aware priors.
raj: propose experiment: 1) disable automated probe for seq<=32 on kv_hot routes (force triton), 2) run A/B for 4h, 3) capture p50/p95 and fallback counts. we can also log sample-weight by kv_hit=true.
perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/inference/routing?canary=1&since=4h -- fallback_count up 3.7x on canary
anya: @rollout please pause the autotune rollout on canary until we validate. small change but impacts tail.
rollout: acknowledged — pausing rollout across canary rings now. will notify infra.
bri: quick note — if we force triton for small seqs, watch for token throughput regressions under heavy batched traffic. batching heuristics might need to allow larger batch accumulation for those cases.
sophia: agreed. experiment plan: start A/B at 1769997900 for 4h, disable probe for seq<=32 on kv_hot in group A, keep group B unchanged, collect p50/p95, fallback_rate, bytes_per_request, kv_hit_rate. I'll post results.
kevin: thanks — I'll add a telemetry flag to capture probe_decision_source per request so we can audit later.
raj: SGTM. if we confirm, next step is to add architecture priors to the kernel cost model (different weights for h100 vs a10) and increase min_samples for short-seq.
sophia: thanks everyone :thumbsup: will follow up with numbers once the AB finishes.
